sense: a general view of a subject

terms.gloss: a view, survey; (in Gellius) a synopsis
evidence: Cic. Brut. 15: ūnō in cōnspectū omnia vidērem
Cic. de Orat. 3.161: in cōnspectū animī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly sight, the range of the eyes (in cōnspectū, in view). The mental survey is rare but good prose; a written synopsis is Gellius’s use (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ut explicātīs ōrdinibus temporum ūnō in cōnspectū omnia vidērem
phrases.english: so that, with the order of the dates laid out, I could see everything in a single survey

sources: Quotations of classical authors checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026) and given in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
